undeclared_returned: The formal 200 response schema is a bare {"type": "object"} with NO properties declared at all - stricter than the 'thin passthrough {status, body}' case flagged in prior batches; here literally nothing is formally typed.

Everything actually returned - top-level 'tags' and 'info', and info's sub-fields 'page', 'page_size', 'count', 'prev', 'next' - is therefore technically undeclared against the formal schema, even though the capability's separate 'returns' hint list (['tags','info','id','name']) loosely anticipates 'tags' and 'info' at the top level.

CAN A TAG BE CREATED? No standalone create-tag capability exists in the searched surface (searchCapability with mode=write over 'create a new tag or add a tag to a test case' surfaced only merge_tags_v1 and update_tag_v1, both of which require an EXISTING tag id). Tags appear creatable only as a side effect of writing a previously-unused string into the `tags` field of a test case (update_test_case_v2 / edit_test_case_v1 / bulk_edit_test_cases[_v2] / create_test_case_v2) or a test run (edit_test_run). This confirms the task's hypothesis: a disposable tag can only be produced indirectly, by tagging an entity, not created directly.

VERDICT RATIONALE: list_tags_v3 itself is UNVERIFIED, not PASS/DRIFT - every entity_type readable in the fixture project returned an empty collection (count:0), so the per-item shape (id, name) promised by the capability's 'returns' hint could never be checked against a real payload. Separately, even a populated response would only yield a hollow PASS: the formal 200 schema is a contentless {"type":"object"} with zero declared properties, so nothing about the response shape is actually pinned down by the contract - see contract.undeclared_returned. And entity_type=test_recording, a value the enum declares as valid, crashes the backend with a persistent 500 (reproduced twice) - a real, reportable drift/bug independent of the empty-collection issue, even though it doesn't change the overall UNVERIFIED verdict for the entity_types that did answer.
